title: The Homecoming of Cedar Falls
premise: Seventeen-year-old Silas Winterbourne has been holding Cedar Falls together since Dad left — cooking, cleaning, and raising his younger siblings while Mom works hospital night shifts. When his best friend Juniper vanishes days before prom, leaving only a ring of keys labeled with the old school annex, Silas discovers she was investigating a decades-old cover-up: the school board knowingly concealed contaminated water in the elementary wing, sickening a generation of kids, including Silas's little brother. As Silas, Juniper's cousin Dee, and a reformed bully-turned-ally dig through sealed records and threaten the wrong powerful families, they realize Juniper didn't run away — she was silenced. In the end, the teens bypass the town's compromised institutions entirely, broadcasting the evidence at prom itself, forcing resignations, an investigation, and a fragile new truth — while Silas finally learns that belonging means letting others carry the weight with him.
about_author: F. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent years covering school board meetings no one attended. They write young adult fiction about ordinary kids who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A chaotic morning routine establishes the Winterbourne household: Silas managing siblings Milo and Wren, Mom asleep after her night shift, and the quiet pride he takes in being 'fine.' Emotional beat: love disguised as control, and the loneliness of competence.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Juniper misses their standing study session; that evening Silas finds her house key, car fob, and a brass key tagged 'ANNEX B' left on his porch with a note reading 'if I'm not back by Friday.' Emotional beat: dread arriving politely, wrapped in routine.

chapters.title: Runaway, Says the Report
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Juniper's cousin Dee arrives from out of town, furious; the sheriff's department files Juniper as a runaway within forty-eight hours. The teens compare notes and find Juniper had been requesting old school records for months. Emotional beat: grief hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Annex B
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Using the brass key, Silas and Dee break into the condemned annex and find Juniper's hidden stash: water test results from 2009 showing lead levels ten times legal limits, plus a list of sickened students. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The List Has Milo's Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Cross-referencing the list, Silas finds Milo — diagnosed with 'unexplained' fatigue two years ago — among the affected children. He hides it from Mom, telling himself he's protecting her. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance, the caretaker's oldest lie.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Cover story chapter: prom planning, small-town texture, and the introduction of board member Councilman Harrow's son, Tate, who seems oddly interested in what the newcomers are asking around school. Emotional beat: surveillance wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The teens track down Ruth Okafor, the retired district clerk whose signature appears on the buried report. She slams the door — but slips a note under it: 'Not everyone signed willingly.' Emotional beat: fear as a language everyone in Cedar Falls speaks fluently.

chapters.title: What Mom Knows
chapters.summary: Mom's POV (a rare shift). A sleepless morning reveals she suspected something years ago and was quietly paid off with a 'settlement' she never read fully. She recognizes Silas's questions before he asks them. Emotional beat: two protectors realizing they've been protecting each other into danger.

chapters.title: Tate Turns
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Tate confronts them, then breaks: his younger sister is on the list too, and his father made him report 'snoopers' at school. He offers the location of the board's off-site records storage. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming a co-conspirator, trust built from shared damage.

chapters.title: Friday Came and Went
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Juniper's deadline passes. The sheriff announces the case is closed as a runaway. Silas publicly loses his composure at a town meeting, drawing Harrow's attention directly onto him. Emotional beat: the mask of 'fine' cracking in public.

chapters.title: Consequences at Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The youngest sibling narrates the fallout: CPS visits after Silas's outburst, Mom's job threatened by Harrow's influence over the hospital board, and Wren quietly hiding evidence in her backpack to keep it safe. Emotional beat: children absorbing adult failures and fighting back in child-sized ways.

chapters.title: Ruth's Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ruth Okafor finally talks: she was pressured to falsify the follow-up inspection, and she kept a signed confession in a safety deposit box — but the bank branch closes permanently Monday. Emotional beat: a clock starting, courage arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: The Records Room Job
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. The crew executes a tense weekend break-in at the storage facility, photographing minutes of closed sessions where the board voted to conceal rather than remediate. They barely escape a security patrol. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins to feel less like a choice than a necessity.

chapters.title: They Found Her Car
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Juniper's car is pulled from the quarry pond — empty. The sheriff calls it an accident; the teens know she never drove near the quarry. Silas realizes someone wanted the search to end. Emotional beat: hope and terror fused; the stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Harrow corners Silas with an offer: full scholarship money, Mom's job secured, Milo's medical bills covered — if the evidence disappears. Silas almost says yes, thinking of his family. Emotional beat: temptation as the true antagonist; integrity priced in dollars.

chapters.title: Where Juniper Hid Herself
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Re-reading Juniper's notes, Dee deciphers a pattern pointing to the abandoned summer camp where they all went as kids. They find Juniper alive — hiding, injured after fleeing a staged accident, gathering final proof. Emotional beat: reunion as catharsis; the missing friend was hunting all along.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours to Prom
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper recounts her escape and reveals the last piece: a recording of Harrow ordering the cover-up's enforcement. But the annex is being demolished Monday, destroying physical evidence unless it's exposed first. Prom is Saturday. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing into a plan with no margin for error.

chapters.title: The Gymnasium Lights
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. During prom, the group hijacks the AV system, projecting the documents and playing the recording to the entire student body, parents chaperoning, and a local news intern Dee tipped off. Emotional beat: triumph and chaos — the truth detonating in the most public room in town.

chapters.title: What the Town Does Next
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Fallout: Harrow arrested, the superintendent resigns, the state opens an investigation, and Milo gets real medical care. But neighbors who enabled the silence glare in grocery aisles. Emotional beat: victory that costs something; justice as a beginning, not an ending.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Mom testifies publicly about the settlement, reclaiming her own complicity and turning it into accountability. Silas watches his mother become something other than exhausted. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed — not of secrets, but of courage.

chapters.title: Cedar Falls, Repopulated
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Weeks later: the annex becomes a memorial garden planned by students, Ruth Okafor is honored, and Dee decides to stay through graduation. Small scenes of repair — casseroles returned, apologies attempted. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt deliberately, brick by brick.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the fall homecoming dance, Silas dances badly with Juniper, lets Wren and Milo see him cry, and accepts help without flinching. Final image: the porch light left on — not as vigil, but welcome. Emotional beat: 'everything is fine' transformed from a lie into a promise kept together.
